_doc.headline_shapes: Each country entry in `countries` carries its headline in one of two shapes, and both are rendered (traced via frontend/src/data.js's mergeFocusConfig and backend/util/focus_config.py's merge_focus_config, kept in sync): (1) a static `headline` string, used verbatim; (2) `headline_name` + `headline_note`, assembled at merge time into the shared headline_intro/{name}/headline_outro template from common.texts.json. A country only needs one of the two shapes, never both — `headline` wins if present, so setting both would silently drop headline_name/headline_note. Interaction-0 countries (UA/BY/RU) carry neither; they have no headline at all.
_doc.permissiveness_levels: The 3 levels (0-2) are an ORDINAL ENUM of display tiers (map fill colour + legend label) chosen editorially, not a monotone 'how permissive' axis. Strategic-dependence detail (e.g. reliance on a country's bases) lives in each country's own headline/reference text, not in a map tier. Key names are load-bearing (read by index elsewhere) and must not be renamed.

1.label: Acted in 2026 to block some overflight

AT.name: Austria
AT.headline_note: Refuses US overflights connected to Iran war operations, the defence ministry told APA on 2 April 2026 — but decides case by case, and approved a US transit to Crete the same day.

BE.name: Belgium
BE.headline: Most flights between UK and German airspace visibly route around Belgium through the Netherlands, with the exception of some shorthaul tactical airlift. Belgium appears to already be largely bypassed.

BG.name: Bulgaria
BG.headline_note: Default route to the theater: almost nine in ten flights leaving Europe to the south-east cross Bulgaria.

CH.name: Switzerland
CH.headline_note: Applies neutrality law case by case: rejected US reconnaissance overflights on 14 March 2026; transport, humanitarian and medical flights permitted.

CZ.name: Czech Republic
CZ.headline_note: On the main route between German bases and the theater (97% of such flights cross it). Not a single point of failure: Poland offers a bypass into Slovakia.

DE.name: Germany
DE.headline_note: Ramstein and Spangdahlem are the two US air bases in use; Ramstein hosts USAFE's only airlift wing and, per press, the control hub for US Middle East operations. If Germany denied, US operations would be severely disrupted.

ES.name: Spain
ES.headline_note: Denied US use of Rota, Morón and Spanish airspace for the Iran operation from the war's first day; Robles called the war «profundamente ilegal y profundamente injusta».

FR.name: France
FR.headline_note:
Allowed US non-combat aircraft to land at Istres from 5 March 2026 («Un avion ravitailleur, c'est une station-service, ce n'est pas un avion de chasse» — Vautrin); reportedly refused Israel-bound US weapons transit in late March.

If countries on the main flight route blocked, France maintaining or tightening its block would become decisive - it is a single point of failure for any European blockade because of its connection to both the Atlantic/North Sea and Mediterranean.

GB.name: United Kingdom
GB.headline_note: Lakenheath and Mildenhall are major USAF bases; the UK allowed US bombers to strike Iranian missile sites from Fairford (Healey, 9 March 2026). Impact of denial would be large.

GR.name: Greece
GR.headline_note: Souda Bay, Crete, is a key US hub: the US Navy calls its pier the Mediterranean's only military deep-water pier able to berth a US nuclear-powered carrier pierside.

HR.name: Croatia
HR.headline: Near-zero overflight due to Swiss, Austrian and Italian restrictions. Could become decisive if Romania, Bulgaria or Greece blocked — transit between Hungary and the Adriatic depends on Slovenia or Croatia. USS Gerald R. Ford stationed off Split for repairs in April 2026, indicating ongoing cooperation.

HU.name: Hungary
HU.headline_note: Single point of failure on the overland corridor: 98% of flights between Germany and Greece, Bulgaria or Romania cross Hungary, and with Austria and Ukraine closed every overland route runs through Slovakia and Hungary.

IE.name: Ireland
IE.headline: Most transatlantic US military flights route around Irish airspace. Shannon Airport is used as a transit hub for US military transports.

IT.name: Italy
IT.headline_note: Refused some US military flights that fell outside the bilateral base agreements, including at Sigonella; other US flights through Italy continued.

KW.name: Kuwait
KW.headline:
On 5 May 2026, Kuwait told the US alongside Saudi Arabia that it could not use Kuwaiti airspace or bases for a planned offensive. The offensive was immediately halted. Both countries reversed course on 7 May, and within hours the US offensive resumed.

This episode demonstrates that any state on a major supply route or with basing on which US operations substantially rely can stop or pause the war — not just Gulf states. The reversal also shows the pressure such states face.

NL.name: Netherlands
NL.headline_note: Flights between British and German bases route through the Netherlands rather than straight over Belgium (95% vs 8%); US tankers have been seen holding east of Eindhoven.

PL.name: Poland
PL.headline: Almost no relevant US military flights transit Polish airspace. Poland is a major staging area for NATO operations involving Ukraine, but the main Iran war route goes through the Czech Republic.

RO.name: Romania
RO.headline_note: Approved on 11 March 2026 a temporary US deployment of aerial-refuelling aircraft and monitoring equipment, described by President Dan as defensive and non-kinetic.

SA.name: Saudi Arabia
SA.headline:
On 5 May 2026, Saudi Arabia told the US it could not use Saudi airspace or bases for a planned offensive. The offensive was immediately halted. Saudi Arabia reversed course on 7 May, and within hours the US offensive resumed.

This episode demonstrates that any state on a major supply route or with basing on which US operations substantially rely can stop or pause the war — not just Gulf states. The reversal also shows the pressure such states face.

SI.name: Slovenia
SI.headline: Virtually no flights* cross Slovenian airspace. Near-zero overflight due to Swiss, Austrian and Italian restrictions. Could become decisive if Romania, Bulgaria or Greece blocked — transit between Hungary and the Adriatic depends on Slovenia or Croatia.

SK.name: Slovakia
SK.headline_note: With Hungary, Slovakia carries every overland route between German and south-eastern airspace while Austria and Ukraine are closed: 97% of flights between Germany and Greece, Bulgaria or Romania cross it.
